🇲🇽📈 <u>SINALOA INDUSTRY GROWS 10.4% — FOUR TIMES THE NATIONAL RATE</u>

Sinaloa posted one of Mexico's strongest industrial performances in April 2026: 10.4% annual growth against a 2.4% national average, according to INEGI's IMAIEF — sixth place nationwide, tied with Yucatán. Construction led with a 24.9% jump, more than double the national 10.5%.

Hidalgo (21.0%), Nayarit (16.2%), Oaxaca (13.1%), Guerrero (11.9%) and Veracruz (11.2%) topped the table — the industrial map is shifting south and toward 4T-governed states.

🇲🇽🥊 <u>PILARES: WHERE CDMX YOUTH TURN WORKSHOPS INTO CAREERS</u>

The 122nd edition of Dialogos PILARES put faces on Mexico City's community-education model. Boxer Miranda González won medals at the indigenous olympiad two years running after training at PILARES: "PILARES has helped me feel that confidence." Leibniz Ramírez trained in image design and now works as a professional colorist. Fernanda Mercado went from free dance workshops to the Ollin Yolliztli Cultural Center.

Free public training, real careers. That's what a city that invests in its youth looks like.
banner: PILARES: YOUTH BUILD CAREERS IN CDMX

🇲🇽🏠 <u>CDMX LAUNCHES FIRST AFFORDABLE RENTAL PROGRAM FOR YOUTH</u>

Mayor Clara Brugada announced Mexico City's first affordable rental housing program: 1,000 homes in 2026, with priority for young people — part of a broader push that includes the universal university scholarship set to reach some 200,000 students this year, plus uniforms and school supplies for 650,000 children with a 704-million-peso investment.

"Education is the most sacred right of youth. May no door of knowledge close to young people, and no dream fade for lack of schools," Brugada said.

🇲🇽🫂 <u>271,000 REPATRIATED MEXICANS RECEIVED WITH DIGNITY</u>

While ICE cages migrants, Mexico built a reception system. The INM has received 271,193 repatriated citizens since January 20, 2025 — 171,508 by land, 99,685 by air on 816 flights — each greeted with food, medical checks, legal orientation and transport to the Mexico Te Abraza program, which has now delivered over 1,567,000 services through 34 federal agencies in 14 states.

"It has been a permanent demand of the President that our Mexican brothers and sisters not be treated as figures or statistics, but be given humane treatment," said commissioner Sergio Salomón Céspedes.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>"WE WON'T BOW OUR HEADS": SHEINBAUM ON US VISA PURGE</u>

President Sheinbaum called Washington's revocation of visas from Morena figures — including AMLO's son — what it is: "a political purpose, more than one of security... a sense of interference in Mexican politics."

She noted the US has presented no evidence against any of the targeted officials. "I always seek the best possible relationship with the United States, for my people, for my homeland — but I'm not going to bow my head. This is not personal. It's a defense of the homeland. We coordinate as equals."

🇲🇽🏭 <u>MEXICO FAST-TRACKS $3.5 BILLION IN PRIVATE INVESTMENT</u>

Mexico's top business chamber confirms the Sheinbaum government's single-window system under Plan Mexico is working: more than $3.5 billion in private projects — national and foreign — already authorized, with energy generation leading the way.

"The projects we've submitted get resolved quickly. Soon we'll have an announcement, because more than $3.5 billion in investments have already been authorized," said CCE president José Medina Mora, citing the May 4 decrees that cut red tape and stopped the SAT from stalling projects.

While Washington bets on tariffs, Mexico is clearing the runway for capital.

🇲🇽🎨 Los Tigres del Norte will join the "México Canta" semifinal in Los Angeles. — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, announcing the August 23 semifinal The binational contest's first-ever US semifinal lands at the Orpheum Theatre on Aug 23 — free entry with registration, broadcast on Canal 22. Los Tigres del Norte — 60M records sold, 6 Grammys, 12 Latin Grammys — will be honored and accompany the 7 Mexican-American semifinalists. The contest promotes new narratives in Mexican music, away from violence and drugs.
